newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico hit by wave of bomb hoaxes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico hit by wave of bomb hoaxes.

text.p: Mexicans, already nervous about a series of attacks by a new band of guerrillas, were hit by a wave of bomb threats on Wednesday, television programme Hechos said.

The threats, which were false alarms, were recorded in the capital, Mexico City, in the popular tourist resort of Acapulco, and in the northern industrial city of Monterrey, the television programme said.
Soldiers and police evacuated a department store in a shopping mall in Acapulco after an anonymous caller warned of a bomb. The Interior Ministry later said the threat was false.
Acapulco is 180 miles (300 km) from Mexico City on the Pacific Coast in the state of Guerrero, a poor and backward region where a new Marxist guerrilla army, the EPR, sprang up at the end of June.
Last week the EPR carried out a series of bloody attacks that left several dead, mainly government security officers.
